events.name: exhaustivity_listener
events.hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions through grammatical exhaustivity rather than recursive mental simulation of a speaker. When hearing a feature word, the listener considers all candidate objects possessing that feature and applies an exhaustification penalty to any referent that also possesses additional unmentioned features in the context. Consequently, objects that are uniquely and exhaustively described by the uttered word are favored over objects with multiple competing features.

events.name: egocentric_speaker_listener
events.hypothesis: Listeners assume the speaker is egocentric rather than communicative: when referring to an object, the speaker simply samples uniformly from among that object's true features, and the listener inverts this generative model to favor referents with fewer total features. This mechanism disagrees most sharply with depth-2 RSA on complex reference displays where one referent has an alternative feature shared with a distractor while another referent has a unique alternative feature: recursive RSA predicts a strong pragmatic preference for the former, whereas the egocentric speaker listener predicts exact 50/50 indifference because both referents possess the same number of features.

events.name: costly_alternative_speaker
events.hypothesis: Speakers incur a communicative cost for choosing an utterance that is less informative than the best available alternative describing their intended referent. Pragmatic listeners invert this cost-sensitive speaker, reasoning that hearing an ambiguous word implies the speaker lacked a more informative alternative for that referent.

events.name: rsa_l2_shared_prior
